_note: THE APPROVAL SIGNATURE CORPUS (studio-apps.md §11, T5): the canonical bytes and the Ed25519 round-trip, two runners on day one - TS (packages/cli/test/studio-apps-approval.test.ts) and ruby (ClosedSource/scripts/sign_app_approval.rb --self-test) - because a signature format with one implementation is a format nobody has checked (the entitlement N-implementations lesson). THE KEYPAIR HERE IS THE DEV FIXTURE, public on purpose: it is the private half of support/apps-shelf-key.json and approves nothing real; the production key is minted offline at the owner ceremony and never appears in this repository. canonicalBytes law: top-level keys sorted, `signature` excluded, JSON.stringify/JSON.generate semantics (the entitlement rule verbatim), PLUS `grants` sorted inside the bytes so two honest signers of one review cannot disagree over array order. Ed25519 is deterministic (RFC 8032), so the ruby signer's output must BYTE-MATCH `record.signature` - a mismatch is a canonicalization drift, the exact defect this corpus exists to catch.

keys._note: DEV FIXTURE KEYPAIR - see the corpus _note. Never sign a real approval with this.

cases.name: a widened grant refuses - the reviewed set is the signed set
a different tree refuses - the review covered these bytes and no others
a re-ordered grants array still verifies - the canonical bytes sort it
a truncated signature refuses before any crypto runs
